title: Throughput Fingerprinter & Adaptive Health Watches for Private Deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a lightweight 'throughput fingerprinter' that profiles steady-state token throughput and surface workload shifts, and build adaptive health watches that combine latency, error rate, saturation, and token throughput signals to drive automated remediation and safer rollbacks for Private (VPC) deployments. The goal is to reduce false-positive degradations, accelerate detection of real saturation events, and integrate the checks as part of Terraform-deployed stacks so upgrades and autoscaling can gate on proven health signals.
tasks: Design throughput fingerprinter algorithm and storage schema (low-cardinality metrics).
Add runtime exporter for per-deployment throughput histograms and drift counters.
Create adaptive watch engine: composite alerts that weigh latency p50/p95, error-rate delta, and fingerprint drift.
Terraform module changes: inject health-watch configs and SLO thresholds into private deployment module.
Canary rollouts: wire adaptive watches to canary evaluation pipeline and automated rollback hooks.
Rollout docs and runbook update for SRE/solutions engineering.
End-to-end QA in staging with synthetic traffic patterns and tenant-mix scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: Throughput fingerprinter runs with <5ms overhead and stores one 6-hour rolling fingerprint per deployment.
Adaptive watch fires fewer than 2 false-positive rollbacks per 30 days in staging stress tests.
Terraform module exposes healthwatch config that can be toggled per-environment without code changes.
Automated rollback successfully reverts canary on sustained composite alarm for >5 minutes in test harness.
Dashboards and alert runbooks published and linked from deployment console.
design_notes: Favor low-cardinality telemetry to avoid metric explosion across many private VPCs.
Fingerprint uses exponentially weighted moving averages on throughput and a simple hash of request-size distribution to detect shifts, not full payload sampling.
Composite thresholds use a short window (30s) for latency spikes plus a medium window (5m) for sustained saturation — tuned to avoid noisy autoscaling reactions.

Trade-off: aggressive sensitivity catches regressions faster but risks rollback churn. Default configuration will bias stability for enterprise customers and provide opt-in aggressive mode for startups.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge runtime exporter and Terraform module PRs behind feature flag.
2) Deploy to staging and validate against synthetic tenant mixes (small/medium/large).
3) Enable composite watch for internal customers in controlled canary group (10% of infra).
4) Monitor for 48h; iterate thresholds; expand to 50% then 100% after signoff.
5) Post-rollout retrospective and final runbook publication.
qa_notes: Synthetic tests include bursty chat-like traffic, long-context embedding workloads, and steady high-throughput embedding pipelines.
Observed a 12% better distinguishing signal between saturation and cold-cache-induced latency when combining fingerprint drift with error-rate slope.
Found one false positive tied to mis-labeled egress throttling in staging — added a dependency on egress metrics to the composite rule.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: metric cardinality explosion in large orgs — Mitigation: aggregate at deployment-id and tenant-class only.
Risk: over-enthusiastic rollbacks during transient cloud flaps — Mitigation: require sustained composite alarm for 5m + canary-fallback window before automated rollback.
Risk: operators confused by new health vocabulary — Mitigation: update Console UX with labels and hover help, and host training session.
